text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today after dropping sharply over the past week—down nearly 7% since late October. The stock's steep decline tracks a broader oil price collapse: US oil has tumbled from the mid-$150s range two weeks ago to $99.64 per barrel today, erasing most of the geopolitical premium that pushed prices higher earlier in the fall. Oil refiners and producers like ConocoPhillips earn less profit when crude prices fall, so the stock has followed the commodity down.

The past week's selloff reflects investors pulling back from oil on mixed signals about geopolitical risk. While some analysts argue that renewed U.S.-Iran tensions could push oil back above $100, the market is instead pricing in a possibility of diplomatic progress and unwinding the post-election risk premium that had supported prices. The company's quarterly earnings announcement yesterday doesn't appear to have reversed this sector-wide pressure.
